_comment: Lever library. Each entry replaces a whole line matched by a unique prefix, so a lever stays valid as the winning train.py evolves and its current value changes. 'value' is substituted into 'line'.

seed43.plan: SEED VARIANCE MEASUREMENT (seed 43, not an improvement). Replicates so far hold the seed at 42 and capture only kernel nondeterminism and step jitter; this additionally varies initialisation and data order, which is the variance that decides whether a lever generalises. If this scores below the incumbent that is a lucky draw, NOT a win — the reference repo's own published run lists 'random seed 42->137' as a kept improvement, which is this exact failure mode.

cmp_mlp5_d9.plan: CONSTANT-CAPACITY SHAPE: MLP 4x -> 5x with DEPTH 10 -> 9 (~88M vs 85.9M, width stays 640). Fatter MLP, fewer layers - the opposite allocation to cmp_mlp3_d12.

cmp_deep_narrow.plan: CONSTANT-CAPACITY SHAPE (corrected): DEPTH 12 with ASPECT_RATIO 48 to hold model_dim at 640, plus MLP 4x -> 3x. ~91M vs 85.9M. Replaces cmp_mlp3_d12, which unintentionally widened to 768 and landed at 121M.

cmp_mlp3_d12.plan: CONSTANT-CAPACITY SHAPE: MLP 4x -> 3x with DEPTH 10 -> 12 (~91M vs 85.9M). Leaner MLP, more layers. Both changes lost alone; the question is whether the parameters are better spent on depth than on MLP width at fixed total.
cmp_mlp3_d12.closed_reason: MIS-DESIGNED: landed at 121.1M, not the intended ~91M — DEPTH 12 also widens model_dim to 768 via ASPECT_RATIO. Lost +0.0065, but does not test what it claimed

qknorm_off.plan: Remove QK normalisation before attention. A load-bearing primitive like the relu-squared activation, never varied; worth knowing whether it earns its cost.
qknorm_off.closed_reason: removing QK norm lost +0.0147 despite +4% steps and higher MFU

relu_cubed.plan: MLP activation relu-squared -> relu-cubed. GeLU lost 0.0254, so the squaring is doing real work; this probes whether the exponent itself is tuned.
relu_cubed.closed_reason: relu-cubed lost +0.0101; with gelu at +0.0254, relu-squared is bracketed

dbs64.line: DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE = 64  # per-device batch size (reduce if OOM)
dbs64.plan: DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE 128 -> 64 at unchanged TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE, so grad_accum_steps goes 1 -> 2. Same optimizer batch, different micro-batching: a pure throughput/memory probe.

matmul_highest.plan: float32 matmul precision high -> highest. Trades throughput for numerical precision in the fp32 paths; untested.

rt_batch19.plan: RETEST at the current operating point: TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE 2**18 -> 2**19. The batch optimum was fixed before the RoPE, embedding-LR, final-LR and weight-decay wins existed; this is the campaign's largest lever and the one most worth re-probing for interaction.
rt_batch19.closed_reason: 2**19 lost +0.0179 at the current operating point — no interaction, closure confirmed

subs: DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE = 64  # per-device batch size (reduce if OOM)
rt_batch17.plan: RETEST: TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE 2**18 -> 2**17 with DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE 64 to keep grad_accum at 1. Probes the other side of the batch axis at the current operating point.
rt_batch17.closed_reason: 2**17 lost +0.0045 at the current operating point — batch 2**18 bracketed again

rt_depth12.plan: RETEST: DEPTH 10 -> 12 at the current operating point. Capacity lost at 135M when tested against the old configuration; the LR set has changed substantially since.
rt_depth12.closed_reason: DEPTH 12 lost +0.0095 at 135.3M — capacity ceiling confirmed post-RoPE

rt_width768.plan: RETEST: width 640 -> 768 at DEPTH 10 and the current operating point. Lost by 0.0036 against the old configuration.
rt_width768.closed_reason: width 768 lost +0.0053 and +0.0052 on two runs at the current operating point

mlp3.plan: MLP expansion 4x -> 3x. Cuts MLP FLOPs ~25%, trading capacity for steps - the capacity/throughput tradeoff at a different lever than DEPTH.
mlp3.closed_reason: 3x lost +0.0036 and +0.0028 on two parents despite +10% steps

mlp5.plan: MLP expansion 4x -> 5x, bracketing the ratio upward since DEPTH showed capacity pays here.

depth9.plan: DEPTH 10 -> 9. ASPECT_RATIO rounding keeps model_dim at 640, so this is a pure depth change at constant width - the one interior point the earlier sweep skipped.
depth9.closed_reason: DEPTH 9 lost +0.0019 at 80.9M params; DEPTH 10 confirmed optimal at width 640

ve_all.plan: Value embeddings on every layer instead of alternating. Doubles VE coverage; the ResFormer value-residual path has never been varied.
ve_all.closed_reason: value embeddings on all layers lost +0.0040 and added 26M params (85.9 -> 112.1M)

act_gelu.plan: MLP activation relu-squared -> gelu. The activation has been fixed since the baseline and is untested.
act_gelu.closed_reason: gelu lost +0.0254 — by far the largest loss of the campaign; relu-squared is load-bearing

rotary4.plan: Rotary table length 10x sequence_len -> 4x. Pairs with the RoPE base-frequency win; the table extent is a separate untested knob.
rotary4.closed_reason: rotary table 4x lost +0.00062; the 10x extent stands

head64.line: HEAD_DIM = 64           # target head dimension for attention
head64.plan: Attention expressivity at constant FLOPs: HEAD_DIM 128 -> 64 doubles the head count at the same model_dim. Same parameter count, same matmul cost, more independent attention subspaces.

span4.plan: Attention span seq/8 -> seq/4. The span was tuned at the old 50.3M shape, and seq/8 was never established over seq/4 (1 sigma).

span2.plan: Attention span back to the original seq/2. Tests whether the span cut still pays at the larger shape with far fewer steps.
span2.closed_reason: seq/2 is the baseline span, superseded

mlr03.line: MATRIX_LR = 0.03        # learning rate for matrix parameters (Muon)
mlr03.plan: MATRIX_LR 0.04 -> 0.03. Raising to 0.05 lost 0.0011 (~7 sigma), so if the optimum moved it moved down.

aspect72.plan: Width sweep at fixed DEPTH 10, wider: model_dim 640 -> 768 (6 heads). Separates width from depth, which the DEPTH knob confounds via rounding.

aspect48.plan: Width sweep at fixed DEPTH 10, narrower: model_dim 640 -> 512 (4 heads). With the 768 probe this gives three points at constant depth.

wd01.line: WEIGHT_DECAY = 0.1      # cautious weight decay for Muon
wd01.plan: WEIGHT_DECAY 0.2 -> 0.1. The run is sub-single-epoch so there is little to regularise against; less decay may leave more capacity usable.
wd01.closed_reason: reverting 0.15 -> 0.1 lost +0.0019 on the current lineage

unemb006.plan: UNEMBEDDING_LR 0.004 -> 0.006. The embedding LR responded strongly to being raised; the unembedding is the paired Adam group and may too.

scalar07.line: SCALAR_LR = 0.7         # learning rate for per-layer scalars (Adam)
scalar07.plan: SCALAR_LR 0.5 -> 0.7. Same reasoning as the embedding LR: fewer total steps means each Adam group gets less total movement.

warmup005.line: WARMUP_RATIO = 0.05     # fraction of time budget for LR warmup
warmup005.plan: WARMUP_RATIO 0.0 -> 0.05. No warmup at all is unusual; at a larger model and higher embedding LR a short warmup may stabilise early steps.

finallr01.line: FINAL_LR_FRAC = 0.1     # final LR as fraction of initial
finallr01.plan: FINAL_LR_FRAC 0.0 -> 0.1. Decaying fully to zero wastes the last steps; a nonzero floor keeps them useful.

pattern8.line: WINDOW_PATTERN = "SSSSSSSL" # sliding window pattern: L=full, S=short context
pattern8.plan: WINDOW_PATTERN SSSL -> SSSSSSSL: only 1 layer in 8 attends to full context instead of 2 in 4.
pattern8.closed_reason: SSSSSSSL lost twice (+0.0025, +0.0025) on two different parents

emb12.line: EMBEDDING_LR = 1.2      # learning rate for token embeddings (Adam)
emb12.plan: Push the embedding-LR axis further to 1.2.
emb12.closed_reason: EMBEDDING_LR optimum is near 0.8-0.9; 1.0 already overshot

emb09.line: EMBEDDING_LR = 0.9      # learning rate for token embeddings (Adam)

warmdown07.line: WARMDOWN_RATIO = 0.7    # fraction of time budget for LR warmdown
warmdown07.plan: WARMDOWN_RATIO 0.5 -> 0.7 (MORE cooldown). Corrects a premature closure: I tested only 0.35, saw it lose, and declared 0.5 optimal from a one-sided test. The untested direction is up.
warmdown07.closed_reason: 0.7 lost +0.00042; with 0.35 also losing, 0.5 is bracketed

unemb008.plan: UNEMBEDDING_LR 0.004 -> 0.008. Same family as the embedding LR, which was the campaign's clearest knob win.

rope50k.plan: RoPE base frequency 10000 -> 50000. A longer rotary wavelength changes how positions are encoded across the 2048-token context; untouched so far and structurally independent of every axis tested.

rope100k.plan: RoPE base frequency -> 100000, continuing the axis if 50000 pays.
rope100k.closed_reason: 100000 lost +0.00153 against the 50000 win; axis peaks at 50k

x0_005.plan: x0_lambda init 0.1 -> 0.05. These per-layer scalars gate how much of the embedding output is re-injected at each block; the init sets where that mixing starts.
x0_005.closed_reason: 0.05 lost on two parents (+0.00124, +0.00169); gating init does not want lowering

span16.plan: Attention span seq/8 -> seq/16 (128 tokens). seq/8 beat seq/4 by ~11 sigma at this shape, so the axis is still live and needs bracketing from below.

wd005.line: WEIGHT_DECAY = 0.05     # cautious weight decay for Muon
wd005.plan: WEIGHT_DECAY 0.1 -> 0.05. 0.2 -> 0.1 won, so bracket below before closing the axis.
wd005.closed_reason: 0.05 lost +0.00116; weight decay does not want lowering below 0.1

wd015.line: WEIGHT_DECAY = 0.15     # cautious weight decay for Muon
wd015.plan: WEIGHT_DECAY 0.1 -> 0.15, filling in between the tested 0.1 and 0.2.
wd015.closed_reason: 0.15 tied 0.1 within noise (+0.00018 = ~1.2 sigma); axis flat, incumbent stands

scalar03.line: SCALAR_LR = 0.3         # learning rate for per-layer scalars (Adam)
scalar03.plan: SCALAR_LR 0.5 -> 0.3. Raising to 0.7 lost, so if the optimum moved it moved down.
scalar03.closed_reason: 0.3 lost +0.0051; with 0.7 also losing, SCALAR_LR 0.5 is bracketed

rope200k.plan: RoPE base frequency -> 200000, the far end of the axis.
rope200k.closed_reason: further out than the losing 100000; not worth a trial

x0_015.plan: x0_lambda init 0.1 -> 0.15, bracketing the residual-gating init upward.
x0_015.closed_reason: 0.15 lost +0.0020; with 0.05 also losing, x0_lambda 0.1 is bracketed

finallr005.line: FINAL_LR_FRAC = 0.05    # final LR as fraction of initial
finallr005.plan: FINAL_LR_FRAC 0.0 -> 0.05, a gentler nonzero floor than 0.1.

betas9.plan: ADAM_BETAS beta1 0.8 -> 0.9. Both Adam-group LRs paid; the Adam momentum is untested.

betas7.plan: ADAM_BETAS beta1 0.8 -> 0.7, bracketing Adam momentum downward.
betas7.closed_reason: beta1 0.7 lost +0.0034; with 0.9 also losing, beta1 0.8 is bracketed

unemb005.plan: UNEMBEDDING_LR 0.006 -> 0.005, refining between the tested 0.004 and 0.006.

emb085.line: EMBEDDING_LR = 0.85     # learning rate for token embeddings (Adam)
emb085.plan: EMBEDDING_LR fine probe at 0.85, between the 0.8 and 0.9 results.

mlr035.line: MATRIX_LR = 0.035       # learning rate for matrix parameters (Muon)
mlr035.plan: MATRIX_LR 0.04 -> 0.035. Both 0.03 and 0.05 failed to beat 0.04; this probes finer.

muon500.plan: Muon momentum warmup stretched from 300 to 500 steps. The schedule was set for a ~1000-step run; this one does ~1310.

muon150.plan: Muon momentum warmup shortened to 150 steps, bracketing the schedule downward.
muon150.closed_reason: warmup 150 tied within noise (+0.00022); default 300 stands

rope25k.plan: RoPE base 50000 -> 25000, refining between the winning 50000 and the baseline 10000.
rope25k.closed_reason: 25000 lost +0.0028; RoPE peak is sharp at 50000

rope75k.plan: RoPE base 50000 -> 75000, refining between the winning 50000 and the losing 100000.

finallr0025.line: FINAL_LR_FRAC = 0.025   # final LR as fraction of initial
finallr0025.plan: FINAL_LR_FRAC 0.05 -> 0.025. 0.05 beat both 0.0 and 0.1, so the optimum is inside (0, 0.1).

finallr0075.line: FINAL_LR_FRAC = 0.075   # final LR as fraction of initial
finallr0075.plan: FINAL_LR_FRAC 0.05 -> 0.075, bracketing the winner from above.

emb095.line: EMBEDDING_LR = 0.95     # learning rate for token embeddings (Adam)
emb095.plan: EMBEDDING_LR 0.9 -> 0.95, refining between the winning 0.9 and the losing 1.0.

betas299.plan: ADAM_BETAS beta2 0.95 -> 0.99. Only beta1 has been probed; beta2 is untouched.
betas299.closed_reason: beta2 0.99 lost +0.0011; 0.95 stands, both betas now bracketed

muonhi.plan: Muon momentum range 0.85->0.95 raised to 0.90->0.98. The endpoints are untested; only the warmup length has been probed.

muonlo.plan: Muon momentum range lowered to 0.80->0.92, bracketing the endpoints downward.
muonlo.closed_reason: momentum range 0.80-0.92 lost +0.00045; default 0.85-0.95 bracketed both sides

wd02.line: WEIGHT_DECAY = 0.2      # cautious weight decay for Muon
wd02.plan: WEIGHT_DECAY 0.15 -> 0.2 on the current lineage. Reverting to 0.1 lost 0.0019 here, which conflicts with the earlier flat reading; this probes the other side.
wd02.closed_reason: 0.2 lost +0.00069; with 0.1 losing +0.0019, WEIGHT_DECAY 0.15 is bracketed on this lineage

_prior_note: Several lever choices below are informed by task/progress.png — the reference repo's own published example run, which is inside this workspace. It is a prior over WHICH levers to try first, not evidence: every claim rests on the measurement taken here. Directions it reports as kept: warmdown up to 0.7, 5% warmup, unembedding LR 0.008, SSSSL window pattern, RoPE base increases, x0_lambda init 0.05.
